examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Secant-Tangent and Other Identities
examples.problem: Express $2\tan x\cdot(\cot x+\tan{x})$ in terms of $\sec x$ only.
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+\tan^2 x = \sec^2{x}
$$

Also, recall the following identity:

$$
\cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \tan x\cdot \cot x = 1
$$

Using the above identities, we can simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{tan}⁡x) & =2\operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡x+2{tan}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2\cdot 1+2{tan}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2\text{ }\,(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2\,{sec}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
2\tan x\cdot(\cot x+\tan{x})= 2\sec^2x.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1} & =\frac{4\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{1+{tan}^{2}⁡x-1} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{{tan}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4\cancel{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{4\operatorname{tan}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x-1}=\frac{4}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.
$$
